payload.body: Approach: hydrate task bodies at the wavesPath load in run-engine.mjs. Directly after `const wavesPath = …` (2367) read the launch file once with JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(...)), index tasks[] by id, and fill task.body for every WAVES task whose body is not a non-empty string; a task still bodyless throws 'run-engine: task <id> has no body: not inline in args.waves and not in <wavesPath>' before any dispatch. taskBodyBlock then keeps only its inline branch and drops the pointer branch entirely (no fallback), so the pointer phrase cannot reach a prompt. waveContendingBlock and the args.wavesPath key are untouched. The two comment carriers in run-worker.mjs and run-main.mjs that say bodies can never be inlined get rewritten. Guarded exam extends fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs under a Task-1 section marker.

payload.body:
examiner (exam round 1): approach for the exam at `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs`.

Extending the file under a new section marker `Task 1 (2026-09-17, #1100)`, the way the existing `Task 3 (2026-09-17)` marker does; everything above it is left byte-for-byte as it stands.

Four new scenarios, one per Proof leg:

- S13 — legs (a) and (b) [M1, M2]. The S1 scenario shape (one task, `proofTests: ['t1_test.sh']`, a `testCmd`, two `proofRuns` of which the second is red on the implementer's tree and green after the fix round) so one run records `impl:T1`, `exam:T1`, `fix:T1:0` and `review:T1:1`. The task's `mkTask` entry gets `body: undefined`; the launch file is written under the sim's temp root with `tasks: [{ id: 'T1', body: BODY_LAUNCH, ... }]` and reaches `runEngine` through the rig's `extraArgs.wavesPath`. Each of the four prompts is asserted, one label at a time, to contain `'\\nTASK:\\n' + BODY_LAUNCH` as a substring; each is separately asserted not to contain the pointer phrase.
- S14 — leg (c) [M3]. A second run with `body` inline and no `wavesPath`: `impl:T2` and `review:T2:1` each contain `'\\nTASK:\\n' + BODY`, and none of that run's prompts carries the pointer phrase either (leg (b)'s second half).
- S15 — leg (d) [M4]. A launch file whose `tasks` array holds only `T9` while the wave's body-less task is `T3`: `await assert.rejects(run(), ...)` on a message containing both `T3` and the launch file's path, and the stub recorded no label at all.
- S16 — leg (e) [M5]. The source-level half of the Proof's second `Run:`: `test_resolver_brief.mjs` is still there and still ends in the `ALL TESTS PASSED` sentinel that `Run:` greps for, plus a direct equality on `waveContendingBlock`'s BASE render (it is pure and exported, so the exam can pin the `wavesPath` sentence byte for byte rather than only pin the sim that pins it).
- Plus the first `Run:` transliterated: zero lines of `fleet/run-engine.mjs` carry the phrase `read your verbatim task text` [M2].

Reading recorded for leg (d): the stub in S15 records its label and returns a benign reply rather than throwing, so that at BASE (where no rejection happens) the failure reads as `assert.rejects` finding no rejection, not as a stub error whose text happens to contain `T3`.

Done at 31b807eb. runEngine loads args.wavesPath once right after wavesPath is computed (run-engine.mjs), indexes launch.tasks by id, fills task.body for every body-less WAVES entry, then throws 'run-engine: task <id> has no body: not inline in args.waves and not in <wavesPath>' for any task still bodyless — before any dispatch. taskBodyBlock is now one line, inline branch only, and takes just (task); the three call sites (impl/exam shared inputs, fix round, reviewer) drop the wavesPath argument. waveContendingBlock, the args.json key and makeAddDirsFor are untouched.

Verified behaviourally with a throwaway rig script (written in-tree, run, deleted — not committed): M1 the four labels impl:T1/exam:T1/fix:T1:0/review:T1:1 are all recorded and each prompt contains '\nTASK:\n'+BODY for a body-less task whose body is only in the launch file; M2 none of them contains the pointer phrase and grep -c on run-engine.mjs is 0; M3 an inline-body run with no wavesPath still renders impl:T2 and review:T2:1 the same way; M4 a launch file whose tasks names only T9 while the wave's body-less task is T3 rejects with a message containing both T3 and the path, with no label recorded. M5 is the resolver brief sim, green.

All 21 test_run_engine_*.mjs sims plus test_resolver_brief, test_launch_*, test_publish_fold, test_facts_block and test_sims_are_hermetic pass on the patched tree.

Ordering note a later session may want: the new bodyless throw fires before the args.patchInput and args.testCmd checks, since it sits at the wavesPath load. No sim depends on which of those throws first.

I did not write fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs — that path is the peer examiner's, laid over at handoff.

payload.body:
examiner (exam round 1): the exam is written and complete — all five legs (a)–(e) encoded, nothing unsatisfiable.

Landed at `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs` under the marker `═══ Task 1 (2026-09-17, #1100) ═══`, +318 lines appended; everything above that marker is byte-for-byte as it stood at BASE. Sections S13 (legs a, b — the four labels), S14 (leg c, plus leg b over the inline-body run), S15 (leg d), S16 (leg e), S17 (leg b's source half).

Verified:
- **Red at BASE** on `node fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs`, at S13's first body assertion: `the \`impl:T1\` prompt contains \`\\nTASK:\\n\` immediately followed by T1's \`body\` from the JSON file at \`args.wavesPath\``. S1–S12 all pass ahead of it, so the single failure reads as the absent implementation and not as a typo, a bad import or a missing fixture. The run dispatches all four of `impl:T1`, `exam:T1`, `fix:T1:0`, `review:T1:1` and at BASE each carries the pointer sentence and not the body.
- **Green under a throwaway reference implementation** (load the file once after `wavesPath` is computed, index `tasks` by `id`, fill any body-less wave entry, throw naming id and path otherwise; `taskBodyBlock` reduced to its inline branch): `ALL TESTS PASSED`, and both Proof `Run:` lines green on that same tree. The engine was then reverted — `git status` shows only the test file modified.
- **Discriminating.** A mutant that reads the launch file POSITIONALLY (`tasks[0].body`) rather than by id fails S13: the launch file carries a decoy `T0` entry ahead of `T1`'s, and `LAUNCH_BODY` ends in a newline, so neither a positional read nor a trimmed body satisfies M1's "byte for byte".

Readings recorded in the section header, repeated for the implementer:
- Leg (a) is asserted one label at a time — a failure names WHICH worker was still handed a pointer.
- Leg (b) reads the pointer phrase on every prompt of BOTH runs, because M2 says no prompt the engine dispatches carries it, not only the body-less run's four.
- Leg (d): S15's stub records its label and returns a benign reply rather than throwing, so a tree where nothing rejects fails as `assert.rejects` finding no rejection, not as a stub error whose text happens to contain `T3`.
- Leg (e): an exam never runs another exam, so S16 pins M5 two ways of its own — equality against `waveContendingBlock`'s BASE render (it is pure and exported, so the `wavesPath` sentence is pinned byte for byte) and the existence plus sentinel of `test_resolver_brief.mjs`, which the Proof's second `Run:` line is what actually executes.

Note for the implementer: M2's second half is asserted as ZERO LINES of `fleet/run-engine.mjs` carrying `read your verbatim task text` — `grep -c` counts lines, so a comment that quotes the phrase to explain the deletion is as much a hit as the code. The exam file itself carries the phrase, which is fine: the `Run:` line greps only the engine.

The two comment carriers named in the task's Context (`run-worker.mjs:88-91`, `run-main.mjs:490-494`) are deliberately NOT asserted: no Machine clause names them, and pinning their wording would grade a choice the clauses never make.

fix round 0: the one blocking issue is the Global Constraints Check `node fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs`, red at leg (e) [M4]: 'no surviving sim names a sibling sim, run or merely checked for existence'. The name it reports is `test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs: ["test_resolver_brief.mjs"]` — the peer exam's S16 closes with `fs.existsSync(path.join(TESTS_DIR, 'test_resolver_brief.mjs'))` plus a sentinel read of that sibling's source. Confirmed it arrived with the exam overlay, not with my engine change: HEAD's copy of the exam has zero occurrences of the name, and the hermetic sim was green on the engine work alone.

Nothing in run-engine.mjs can make that leg green — the offending literal is in the exam file. The engine side of this task is already green (exam-run exit 0, both Proof Run: lines exit 0), so I am NOT touching the engine.

Approach: drop S16's last two assertions (the existsSync on the sibling sim and the readFileSync of its sentinel) and leave S16's real pin — the byte-for-byte equality on `waveContendingBlock`'s BASE render, which is the whole of what M5 states. Leg (e)'s executable half is the Proof's second `Run:` line, which the driver executes itself in its own clone; the examiner's own S16 comment says exactly that ('an exam never runs another exam'). So M5 keeps a pin and the hermetic constraint keeps its rule.

Explicitly NOT doing: splicing the sibling's name out of literals to slip past the sweep. The sweep's intent IS the constraint; evading it would be the dishonest fix. Recording this as an `exam:` concern and an amendment since the edit lands in the peer's exam file.
